samples.question: This image shows one door leaf lying flat on a page. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks just inside it are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. The door leaf is the large solid coloured rectangle. The small dark slate blocks that sit astride one single edge of the leaf, half on the leaf and half off it, are the hinges, and the edge they straddle is the hinged edge; every hinge block in an image is on that one edge. The one solid black disc painted inside the leaf is the handle. Any white bars crossing the leaf are panel grooves and never mark the answer. Now imagine the straight line drawn across the middle of the leaf parallel to the hinged edge: it splits the leaf into a half that touches the hinged edge and a half that does not. The handle belongs to the half that contains the centre of the black disc. Which edge carries the hinges, the leaf's size and shape, where it sits on the page, its colour, the number and size of the hinge blocks, the size of the handle and the number of panel grooves all change from image to image, and the handle need not be placed where a door handle is normally placed. Read only what is painted in this image and do not answer from where handles usually go. Is the handle in the same half of the leaf as the hinged edge, or in the opposite half? Answer with exactly one of: same, opposite.
